source_user: Two serving systems claim different tokens/s. Design a reproducible comparison. Scenario variant 229: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: freeze model revision, tokenizer, precision, hardware, topology, prompt/generation distributions, concurrency, warmup, stopping rules, and telemetry; publish raw request traces.
corrected_answer:
For scenario variant 229, define the comparison before measuring it. Count input, generated, and accepted tokens separately, and state whether rates use completed requests or include retries, cancellations, failures, queueing, batching, network, and wall-clock time. Record request admission, queue, first-token, per-token, completion, retry, cancellation, and failure timestamps. Freeze model and tokenizer revisions, precision, runtime and library versions, drivers, hardware and topology, clocks, serving configuration, decoding and stop rules, prompt/output-length distributions, seeds, concurrency, admission and batching policy, cache state, warmup, test duration, and network path.

Falsifiable hypothesis: the reported tokens/s gap is primarily caused by unequal admission, batching, queueing, or accounting rather than intrinsic decode speed; under the frozen contract and equalized policy, the paired difference will be smaller than a predeclared practical margin. Test it with identical randomized request blocks, repeated paired crossover runs at prespecified offered loads, warmup exclusion, fixed stopping rules, and no unregistered tuning. If the margin or confidence interval contradicts the hypothesis, retain the intrinsic-performance explanation rather than forcing agreement.

Measure generated/input/accepted tokens per second, completed requests/s, TTFT, inter-token and end-to-end latency, queue and service time, p50/p95/p99, errors, timeouts, cancellations, retries, utilization, memory, power/cost, correctness and output quality, plus telemetry completeness. Report units, sample counts, paired effects, uncertainty, exclusions, and saturation points. Publish manifests, raw request traces, seeds, code, and analysis; redact sensitive payloads without changing timing records. Treat platform-specific behavior as unknown until measured. Confounders include clocks and thermal state, kernel/runtime differences, topology, cache warmth, request mix, scheduler interference, backpressure, rate limits, failures, and instrumentation overhead. Before any production or quality-affecting trial, use a canary, rate/load caps, latency/error/quality guardrails, audit logs, and a tested fail-closed rollback; stop on safety, correctness, data-integrity, or resource thresholds and obtain domain-expert review.
